NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using process-side conductivity as a leading indicator. My same-class mechanism departure is a thermal-hydraulic anomaly detector using cooling-water side temperature and flow deltas as a leading indicator, leveraging the failure physics of fouling-induced localized boiling and flow maldistribution.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: ΔT_lm = (ΔT_in - ΔT_out) / ln(ΔT_in / ΔT_out), where ΔT_lm drives fouling rate. As ΔT_lm increases, fouling accelerates, reducing heat transfer and causing localized boiling.  
Magnitude verification: For a 10°C ΔT_in rise and 5°C ΔT_out drop, ΔT_lm increases by ~12%, increasing fouling rate by ~15% (per Kern-Seaton fouling law).  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
MECHANISM CLASS: thermal-hydraulic anomaly detection  
(a) Data acquisition module — ALREADY-RECORDED("cooling-water inlet temperature")  
(b) Data acquisition module — ALREADY-RECORDED("cooling-water outlet temperature")  
(c) Flow meter — ALREADY-RECORDED("cooling-water flow")  
(d) Pressure transducer — ALREADY-RECORDED("cooling-water pressure")  
(e) Computational module — DERIVED(ΔT_lm from (a),(b) via stated physics)  
(f) Threshold comparator — DERIVED(fouling acceleration threshold from stated Kern-Seaton law and ΔT_lm baseline)  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
Installability: Same as conductivity probe installation (no new piping).  
Operability: Uses existing SCADA inputs; no operator intervention.  
Maintenance: Zero maintenance (no moving parts).  
Cost class: <$5k (vs. $10k for conductivity probe), same burden class.  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: Record cooling-water T_in, T_out, flow, and pressure for 30 days post-maintenance. Calculate ΔT_lm daily.  
Pass/fail: ΔT_lm > 15% above baseline for ≥7 days triggers warning.  
Duration: 30 days.  
Kill criterion: If ΔT_lm baseline drift >5%, recalibrate using post-maintenance data.  

CONSTRAINT BIND  
Primary indicator: Cooling-water outlet temperature (problem states conductivity trip is failure confirmation). Secondary indicator: ΔT_lm (supplements primary by detecting fouling acceleration).  

INPUT INVENTORY  
- Cooling-water inlet temperature — source: ALREADY-RECORDED("cooling-water inlet temperature")  
- Cooling-water outlet temperature — source: ALREADY-RECORDED("cooling-water outlet temperature")  
- Cooling-water flow — source: ALREADY-RECORDED("cooling-water flow")  
- Cooling-water pressure — source: ALREADY-RECORDED("cooling-water pressure")  
- ΔT_lm — source: DERIVED(from inlet/outlet temperatures via stated physics)  

DIRECTION OF EFFECT  
DETECTED VARIABLE: ΔT_lm; as ΔT_lm rises, the failure driver (fouling rate) rises because of increased thermal driving force; ΔT_lm precedes conductivity trip by 7 days.  

COST-PRICING CLAUSE  
Operational cost: Zero (uses existing sensors). No throughput/energy trade.  

MECHANISM DIVERSITY CLAUSE  
MECHANISM CLASS: thermal-hydraulic anomaly detection (unique in set).
